questions.question: Discuss "social engineering attacks" and explain how a hacker can use them to gain access.
questions.solution_html:
• A hacker identifies the target, scans for vulnerabilities, uses a known exploit, gains
  • access, escalates privileges, and maintains access. Prevention includes patching, updates
  • firewalls, and antivirus.
  • Xmas Scan
  • Rule-based Attack
  • Tools
  • • John the Ripper
  • • Hashcat
  • • Ophcrack
  • Advantages
  • • No risk of account lockout.
  • • Faster than online attacks.
  • • Can use GPU acceleration.
  • Prevention
  • • Use strong, unique passwords.
  • • Enable Multi-Factor Authentication.
  • • Use salted password hashes.
  • • Implement secure password policies.
  • • Use modern hashing algorithms such as bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2.
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: • Use modern hashing algorithms such as bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2.

questions.question: Differentiate DNS, IP, and HTTPS sniffing in detail and illustrate their attack scenarios.
questions.solution_html:
• DNS sniffing: capture queries/responses; risks (hostnames, subdomains)
  • spoofing/poisoning angle.
  • IP sniffing: passive capture at L3/L2; unencrypted protocols; ARP poisoning to get
  • in-path; session hijack risk.
  • HTTPS sniffing: normally protected; scenarios where visible (misconfig, SSL
  • stripping, rogue CA, compromised proxy); HSTS role.
  • Tools: Wireshark, tcpdump, mitmproxy, Ettercap.
  • Mitigations: encryption, DNSSEC/DoT/DoH, ARP inspection, switch port security
  • HSTS, certificate pinning.
  • For 13–15: clear distinctions, one scenario each, tool + countermeasure per type.
  • CEH Sybex: Ch.6 pp.158–166 (sniffing, ARP, DNS), Ch.7 hijacking.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: CEH Sybex: Ch.6 pp.158–166 (sniffing, ARP, DNS), Ch.7 hijacking.
